clinics.name: BioXcellerator
clinics.district: Medellín (El Poblado, El Tesoro Torre Médica 2, Office 944, Carrera 25A No. 1A Sur-45)
specialties: Wharton's jelly mesenchymal stem cell infusions
clinics.namedDoctors: Karolynn Halpert, MD (founder and general manager; emergency medicine, master's in health administration); Leonardo Ramírez, MD (medical director; emergency medicine); Lucas López Quiceno, MD, MSc (scientific director; epidemiology); Valentina Mesa Pietralunga, MD (IV drips, hyperbaric and ozone; training in functional medicine and homotoxicology); Andrea Gómez Montero, MD, MSc (epidemiology; regulatory liaison with INVIMA); Luz Adriana Palacio, MD, MSc; Juan Pablo Vélez, MD and Juan Pablo Reyes, MD (general practitioners). A Medellín Health City cluster guide names Víctor Gómez Calderín as scientific director. No anesthesiologist named.
clinics.credentials: Self-stated REPS habilitación code 0500116565 and NIT 901.074.877-8 on the Colombian site; REPS public consultation blocked automated reading on October 30, 2026, so the code is unverified. The company states INVIMA certification in Good Clinical Practice for research and an in-house ethics committee; the cluster guide also lists it as an IPS and research centre with GCP certification. El Colombiano reported on October 7, 2020 that INVIMA approved (Resolución 2020029493) a clinical trial of mesenchymal stem cells for COVID-19 run with Clínica Somer, with BioXcellerator supplying cultured umbilical-cord cells. INVIMA's position: a November 2016 INVIMA presentation concluded that advanced cell therapies do not fit Colombia's existing categories (medicines, anatomical components, medical devices) and called for a specific regulation and GMP standards for processing labs; no later INVIMA authorization pathway for commercial stem cell treatments was found. The first page of INVIMA's health-alert index (October 30, 2026) showed no alert naming the company; a keyword search of the alert archive could not be run. The main .com site blocked automated reading (HTTP 403).
clinics.cautions: The cell products are not FDA-approved and Colombia has no specific marketing authorization for commercial mesenchymal stem cell therapies (invima-2016). Clinical benefit claims for the IV formulations on the site are presented without cited studies. A medical-tourism blog claims the company received an FTC COVID-19 warning letter; the FTC's coronavirus warning-letter page does not list the company, so that claim is unverified (ftc-covid-letters). No press report of a death, lawsuit or sanction was found in the searches run (biox-press-elcolombiano, biox-cmhc).
clinics.publishedPrices: Not published on its site. A medical-tourism marketplace article (May 2026) gives Medellín market ranges of $4,500 to $6,500 for a 100-million-cell IV protocol and $8,000 to $12,000 for 200-million-plus cells; these are marketplace ranges (indicative), not the clinic's prices.

clinics.credentials: Legal entity, NIT and REPS code not shown; REPS consultation blocked automated reading on October 30, 2026. The site states that medical evaluation, diagnosis and procedures are provided by allied independent physicians and that Lumm coordinates the patient experience. It describes an in-house laboratory operating under 'GMP standards' with more than 15 characterization tests per batch and a per-patient quality certificate, but names no certifying body and makes no INVIMA statement. It states it does not treat cancer, advanced neurodegenerative disease, type 1 diabetes or severe autoimmune disease.
clinics.cautions: No Colombian marketing authorization pathway exists for commercial mesenchymal stem cell products (invima-2016). The independent-provider structure means the treating physician, not Lumm, is the responsible provider. Laboratory claims are self-reported.
